clauses.title: FRS 102 Overview - True and fair view, consistency and disclosures
clauses.body: Financial statements should present a true and fair view. Accounting policies should be applied consistently and disclosures should be sufficient for users to understand the entity’s financial position and performance.

clauses.title: Section 3 - Financial Statement Presentation (general)
clauses.body: Entities should present a complete set of financial statements with appropriate notes. Presentation and classification should be consistent from period to period unless a change is justified and disclosed.

clauses.title: Section 4 - Statement of Financial Position (general)
clauses.body: Balance sheet items should be classified appropriately between current and non-current where relevant. Key line items should be supported by disclosures for material classes.

clauses.title: Section 5 - Statement of Comprehensive Income and Income Statement (general)
clauses.body: Income and expense items should be presented and classified appropriately. Material items should be disclosed separately, and prior period comparatives included.

clauses.title: Section 7 - Statement of Cash Flows (when required)
clauses.body: A cash flow statement is required for many entities under FRS 102 (subject to exemptions). Classification of cash flows into operating, investing and financing should be consistent and supported by disclosures.

clauses.title: Section 8 - Notes to the Financial Statements (completeness and clarity)
clauses.body: Notes should provide information not presented elsewhere and include accounting policies, critical judgments, key estimates and supporting disclosures for material line items.

clauses.title: Section 10 - Accounting Policies, Estimates and Errors
clauses.body: Material accounting policies should be disclosed. Changes in estimates and corrections of material prior period errors should be disclosed with sufficient detail for users to understand the impact.

clauses.title: Sections 11/12 - Financial Instruments (recognition, measurement, disclosure)
clauses.body: Financial instruments should be recognised and measured in accordance with the relevant sections. Disclosures should explain the nature and extent of risks and the basis for measurement.

clauses.title: Section 13 - Inventories
clauses.body: Inventories should be measured at the lower of cost and estimated selling price less costs to complete and sell. Disclosures should support material inventory classes and valuation policies.

clauses.title: Section 16 - Investment Property
clauses.body: Investment property is generally measured at fair value with changes recognised in profit or loss (with specific exceptions). Disclosures should explain valuation basis and movements.

clauses.title: Section 17 - Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE)
clauses.body: PPE should be recognised at cost (or revalued amount if policy chosen) less depreciation and impairment. Disclosures should support material classes, depreciation methods, and movements.

clauses.title: Section 18 - Intangible Assets other than Goodwill
clauses.body: Intangibles should be recognised when criteria are met and amortised over their useful lives. Disclosures should include amortisation policy, useful lives, and movements for material classes.

clauses.title: Section 19 - Business Combinations and Goodwill
clauses.body: Business combinations require identifiable assets and liabilities to be recognised at fair value at acquisition date. Goodwill is typically amortised. Disclosures should explain key assumptions and movements.

clauses.title: Section 20 - Leases (classification and disclosures)
clauses.body: Leases should be classified and accounted for in accordance with FRS 102. Disclosures should explain lease commitments and the basis for classification where material.

clauses.title: Section 21 - Provisions and Contingencies
clauses.body: Provisions should be recognised when criteria are met and measured reliably. Contingent liabilities and assets should be disclosed where relevant. Disclosures should explain nature and uncertainties.

clauses.title: Section 23 - Revenue (recognition and disclosure)
clauses.body: Revenue should be recognised by reference to the stage of completion of the transaction (where applicable) and when probable economic benefits will flow. Disclosures should explain revenue recognition policies and material judgments.

clauses.title: Section 24 - Government Grants
clauses.body: Government grants should be recognised in accordance with the chosen policy and disclosed appropriately. Disclosures should include nature and extent of grants and accounting treatment.

clauses.title: Section 25 - Borrowing Costs
clauses.body: Borrowing costs are generally recognised as an expense unless capitalisation is permitted and selected. Disclosures should explain policy and material capitalisation amounts.

clauses.title: Section 28 - Employee Benefits (pensions, accruals and disclosures)
clauses.body: Employee benefit costs, including pension obligations, should be recognised appropriately. Disclosures should include significant plans and obligations where material.

clauses.title: Section 29 - Income Tax (current and deferred tax)
clauses.body: Current and deferred tax should be recognised and measured according to the section. Disclosures should explain tax charge composition, deferred tax movements and key reconciliations where required.

clauses.title: Section 30 - Foreign Currency Translation
clauses.body: Foreign currency transactions and balances should be translated and recognised consistently. Disclosures should be provided where material, including the effect of exchange differences.

clauses.title: Section 32 - Events after the end of the reporting period
clauses.body: Adjusting events should be reflected in the financial statements; non-adjusting events may require disclosure. The reviewer should confirm significant events are considered and documented.

clauses.title: Section 33 - Related Party Disclosures
clauses.body: Related party relationships, transactions and balances should be disclosed where required. The reviewer should consider completeness and materiality of related party disclosures.

clauses.title: Going concern - basis of preparation and disclosure (reviewer context)
clauses.body: The reviewer should confirm that going concern has been assessed, the basis of preparation is appropriate, and disclosures are adequate where material uncertainties exist.

clauses.title: Disclosure completeness - material line items and narrative notes
clauses.body: Material balances and transactions should have supporting disclosures. A reviewer should evaluate whether note disclosures and accounting policies provide adequate clarity and completeness for users.
